title: Opening the South Atlantic

labels.title: Seafloor misfit
labels.note: Each isochron: the gap left between its two flanks at its own age. Fracture zones: mean distance to your flowlines.

intro: The South Atlantic is new seafloor, made at the ridge as South America and Africa pulled apart. Isochrons are seafloor of one age, found on both flanks. Pick an isochron: the globe shows the ocean as it was then, and you drag South America (Africa stays put) until the two bold isochrons of that age meet. Fit them one by one, oldest last. Then look at Present: your rotations predict flowlines, and the fracture zones (white) show where the seafloor really went.
questions: Fit C34 (84 Ma), then M0 (120 Ma). Does South America move the same way in both stages?
At Present, do your flowlines follow the fracture zones? Where do they bend, and why?
What would the flowlines look like with only one fitted isochron?
